card.name: Ainu dance
card.tagline: Indigenous Ainu circle and animal-mimicry dances honoring the kamuy
card.profile: Traditional Ainu dance comprises the dances of the Ainu, an Indigenous people living mostly in Hokkaido in northern Japan, performed at ceremonies, banquets and cultural festivals (UNESCO). The traditional style involves a large circle of dancers with onlookers singing accompaniment without instruments; some dances imitate the calls and movements of animals or insects (such as the crane dance, sarorun rimse), others such as the sword and bow dances are rituals (UNESCO). Believing deities dwell in their surroundings, the Ainu use dance to worship and thank nature; it is central to the Iyomante ceremony, in which a bear's embodied deity is sent back to heaven (UNESCO). It was designated an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property in 1984 and inscribed by UNESCO in 2009 (Japan House London).
card.insight: For the Ainu, dance reinforces their connection to the natural and religious world and, per UNESCO, provides a cultural link to other Arctic peoples of Russia and North America (UNESCO).
